content.value: Asynchronous JavaScript supports network requests, delays, and event-driven data. Use async/await to keep code readable and handle errors with try/catch. Never trust an unhandled promise in a production page.

concepts.name: Promise
concepts.description: A JavaScript object representing an asynchronous operation that may complete successfully or fail later.

concepts.name: async/await
concepts.description: JavaScript syntax for writing asynchronous code in a style that reads like sequential steps.

concepts.name: fetch()
concepts.description: A browser API for making network requests and receiving responses.

concepts.name: API request
concepts.description: A request sent to an application programming interface to retrieve or change data.

concepts.name: JSON
concepts.description: A text data format commonly used to exchange structured data between web clients and servers.

concepts.name: Asynchronous callback
concepts.description: A function that runs later after an asynchronous operation or event completes.
